findings.title: Implicit plugin-bearing relocatable inputs now decline final-link reuse
findings.fix: elf_needed no longer accepts ET_REL from its outer ELF header alone. Before returning an empty dynamic dependency list it calls native_relocatable_sections. Direct object/CRT inputs and every understood archive member pass through this same check.
source_evidence: Finite ELF64 little-endian x86_64 ET_REL/header schema, bounded checked section-table and string-table ranges, null section, real NUL-terminated names, fixed cumulative name work and no extended numbering.

GNU LTO/debug-LTO/offload, LLVM/bitcode/plugin and object-only indicators decline. Only understood native section types and finite flags are accepted; unknown types/flags and malformed names/ranges/entry layouts decline.

An unsupported input returns None from dependency discovery, so the ordinary current link runs. The new guard is a conservative reuse admission, not a restriction on language compilation or an attempt to infer missing plugin identity.
findings.tests: The read backend log contains passing native positives, all listed plugin markers in direct objects and archive members, actual Inputs::file direct CRT/archive negatives, unknown section types/flags, raw bitcode, and missing/truncated/malformed section metadata. These are part of 213 passed backend tests.
findings.limits: This closes the demonstrated standard ELF/LTO implicit-plugin omission through conservative admission. It is not a proof for arbitrary externally modified linker/plugin implementations, unsupported object formats or every future extension. Unsupported forms must continue to fall back rather than broaden admission without dependency evidence.

findings.severity: performance/objective limitation, not a safety rejection for ordinary O2
findings.title: Optional whole-transform/stable-name paths can still COW unchanged shared bodies after a private edit
findings.scope: The whole ScalarIdentity transform cache can miss after one changed function. Explicit incremental_o2 fold passes can then mutate unchanged functions again through SharedVec; stable-name closed-executable renaming traverses blocks mutably even when a body needs no operand rename. Those source files are unchanged from e105.
findings.qualification: Ordinary O2 with incremental_o2=false and closed-executable/stable naming disabled does not run those passes. The finding is not evidence of an ordinary-O2 matrix regression. Whole-unchanged fast-path success does not settle genuine private-edit copy cost.
findings.follow_up: Measure complete requests first, then unchanged-body allocations/copies for these explicit modes. Consider per-function transform/rename products or read-only change detection before mutable access if material.
